hints: Start with the first bullet - if a wolf gets one copy from mum and one copy from dad, how many sets of chromosomes does it have in each body cell?
Think about the CPD103 locus - all wolves have the same gene in the same place, but the DNA sequence can vary. What do you call different versions of the same gene?
For the last one, focus on the second bullet - only one copy of the black form is needed for a black coat. Which type of allele shows its effect even when paired with a different allele?
walkthrough:
Two Copies Means Two Sets - Diploid**
You are told wolves inherit two copies of CPD103, one from each parent. That is the definition of diploid. Most animal body cells contain two complete sets of chromosomes, so they have two copies of each gene.

Different Forms - Allele**
The gene locus is the same in all wolves, but the DNA sequence at that locus can differ to give grey or black. Any one of the alternative forms of a gene at the same locus is called an allele.

Shows With Only One Copy - Dominant**
Wolves need only one copy of the black form to be black. That means the black allele masks the other allele in a heterozygote. An allele that is expressed in the phenotype in the heterozygous genotype is dominant.
Final answer: an organism with two copies of each gene - diploid; a form of a gene - allele; a form of a gene that gives a phenotypic effect in a heterozygote - dominant (allele).

walkthrough:
Set Up The Selection Pressure**
CDV causes serious lung disease, so it can kill wolves. That makes CDV a selection pressure. Where dogs are numerous, in the south, transfer to wolves is higher, so wolves in the south face more CDV infection than wolves in the north.

Link Black Coat To Survival**
You are told the protein coded for by the CPD103 gene also defends against infectious lung disease. So the DNA / allele for black coat gives resistance to CDV. When CDV is common, having the black allele gives a selective advantage.

Differential Survival And Reproduction**
In the south, black wolves are more likely to survive CDV than grey wolves. Survivors are more likely to breed and reproduce. Grey wolves are more likely to die before reproducing. This is directional selection favouring black.

Change In Allele Frequency To The South**
Because black survivors reproduce, they pass on the black allele to offspring. Over generations the frequency of the black allele increases in southern populations. That is why the relative frequency of black compared to grey wolves increases from north to south.

Final answer: CDV acts as a selection pressure; the allele for black coat gives resistance to CDV / selective advantage where CDV is common. In the south there is more CDV infection in wolves from dogs; black wolves are more likely to survive and reproduce than grey wolves; so they pass on and increase the frequency of the black allele in the south.

walkthrough:
Describe The Pattern In Fig. 4.1**
The line of best fit rises steadily from left to right. As the percentage of wolves with anti-CDV antibodies increases from near 0 to about 40%, the percentage of black wolves increases from near 0 to about 55%. That is a positive linear correlation, a direct relationship.

Interpret What Antibodies Mean**
Wolves that have been previously infected by CDV have anti-CDV antibodies. So only wolves that were exposed and survived will later have antibodies in their blood. A population with a high % with antibodies is a population that has experienced a high level of CDV.

Explain Why High CDV Means More Black Wolves**
The allele / protein that gives black coat also defends against CDV and helps survival. In a high-CDV population, grey wolves without resistance are more likely to die, while black wolves survive. So after selection, more black wolves are left to count.

Put Description And Reason Together**
Do not claim black coat causes antibody production. The correlation exists because both high antibodies and high % black are results of high CDV exposure plus selection. High disease selects for the resistant black genotype, and survivors carry antibodies as evidence of that disease history.

Final answer: Positive linear correlation - as % with anti-CDV antibodies increases, % of black wolves increases. Wolves that survive CDV later have antibodies; high % antibodies indicates high level of CDV in that population; in such populations grey wolves have died leaving more black wolves; the gene / allele for black coat gives resistance to CDV aiding survival.
